justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are fulfilled: Video Consultation Service handles consultations (R-01), E-Prescription & Interoperability Gateway handles pharmacy integration (R-02), AI Symptom Checker Service provides urgency triage (R-03), and Consent Management Service enforces granular data sharing rules (R-04).
justifications.performance_efficiency: Performance is achieved via asynchronous Cloud Pub/Sub decoupling, ONNX Runtime for low-latency ML inference, PgBouncer database connection pooling, read replicas, and client-side PWA caching (IndexedDB/Hive) to minimize redundant roundtrips.
justifications.compatibility: The E-Prescription & Interoperability Gateway explicitly includes a US FHIR Adapter Component handling HL7 FHIR bundles and an EU Translation Adapter Component for national standards, seamlessly interfacing with External Pharmacies and National Health Systems.
justifications.usability: Both Patient and Clinician personas are served by dedicated interfaces in Web Application and Mobile App, featuring localized routing, session handlers, and tailored workflows such as the Clinician Dashboard and Patient Portal UI.
justifications.reliability: The Bandwidth Adaptator and Video Client Wrapper dynamically degrade streams below 300 kbit/s. Offline Cache & Sync Manager, Resilience & Fallback Handler, and Outbound Resilience & Retry Component provide robust fault tolerance and store-and-forward recovery.
justifications.security: Security is thoroughly addressed via Cloud Armor, Data Residency Enforcement Middleware, Row-Level Security, regional Cloud SQL isolation, CMEK encryption, and cryptographic hash chaining in the Log Integrity Verifier for HIPAA, GDPR, and EU MDR accountability.
justifications.maintainability: High maintainability through modular, domain-driven microservices. Dedicated adapters (e.g., US FHIR and EU Translation Adapters) decouple external variations, while components have clear, single responsibilities connected through standard interfaces (gRPC, mTLS, Pub/Sub).
justifications.portability: The design matches the specified GCP target regions (europe-west3 and us-central1) using geo-routing and regional instances. However, deep integration with GCP-specific managed services (Cloud Armor, Cloud DNS, Pub/Sub) introduces minor friction for non-GCP migration.

PERF-01.justification: The architecture incorporates a dedicated WebRTC SFU node, dynamic bandwidth adaptation, and PgBouncer connection pooling to support high session counts. However, specific SFU horizontal autoscaling and clustering mechanisms across regional nodes are not fully detailed.
elements: Google Cloud Global HTTPS Load Balancer
sensitivity_points: LiveKit SFU node capacity and CPU utilization under concurrent video streams
tradeoffs: SFU media routing improves client bandwidth efficiency but increases cloud compute resource load

PERF-02.justification: A load of 50,000 requests per hour is approximately 14 requests per second. The Python/FastAPI service leverages an ONNX Runtime inference engine and offloads audit logging asynchronously to Google Cloud Pub/Sub, easily meeting the sub-3-second latency requirement.
sensitivity_points: Execution latency of ONNX Runtime models under parallel processing loads
tradeoffs: Asynchronous audit logging over Pub/Sub maximizes throughput at the expense of eventual consistency

AVAIL-01.justification: The Video Client Wrapper, Mobile Video Module, and SFU Bandwidth Adaptator provide dynamic simulcast layer adaptation for low-bandwidth connections. The Offline Cache & Sync Manager queues notes in IndexedDB/SQLite, preventing call termination and ensuring no clinical notes are lost.
sensitivity_points: Simulcast switching latency when network throughput drops below 300 kbit/s
tradeoffs: Degrading to audio-only prioritizes call continuity over clinician visual feedback

AVAIL-02.justification: The target cloud specifies only us-central1 and europe-west3. Since data residency strictly forbids moving US patient data to the EU, a total outage of us-central1 leaves no secondary US failover region defined, making automated recovery within 1 hour unachievable without cold regional provisioning.
sensitivity_points: Single US region deployment creates a single point of failure for US availability
tradeoffs: Operating a single US region minimizes infrastructure costs but sacrifices fast disaster recovery

MOD-01.justification: The E-Prescription Gateway isolates translation logic inside the EU Translation Adapter Component, decoupled from the US FHIR Adapter and core prescription workflows. Adding a new country is confined to this component, though modular country-level plugins are not explicitly separated.
sensitivity_points: Coupling within the EU Translation Adapter when adding distinct national protocol parsers
tradeoffs: Consolidating EU formats into one adapter simplifies service topology but increases regression risk

MOD-02.justification: The AI Symptom Checker Service features a Model Registry Client that supplies versioned model artifacts and handles rollbacks. The Audit & Traceability Component links every inference payload and output to its specific model version ID before publishing immutable logs to Pub/Sub.
sensitivity_points: Atomic model switching and artifact verification in the Model Registry Client
tradeoffs: Recording complete inference inputs and model IDs guarantees MDR compliance but expands storage

SEC-01.justification: The architecture strictly enforces cross-region boundaries through the API Gateway Region Routing Filter, Consent Verification Interceptor, and database-level Row-Level Security. Cross-border requests are blocked without valid consent tokens and logged to pgAudit and the Audit Logging Service.
sensitivity_points: Strict synchronous consent verification prior to evaluating cross-border query routes
tradeoffs: Multi-layered consent and residency validation increases request latency for authorized cross-border clinicians

SEC-02.justification: Consent updates in the Consent Management Service immediately publish events via Pub/Sub. The Cloud SQL container provides Row-Level Security, an Automated Data Purging Daemon, and an In-Database Cryptographic Erasure Engine, ensuring data access ceases immediately and deletion is auditable.
sensitivity_points: Event delivery latency across microservices when processing consent revocation events
tradeoffs: Cryptographic erasure provides verifiable compliance but renders affected data permanently irrecoverable
